narrationScript: Welcome to the second part of our hands-on lab. In this section, you'll modify the `index()` route in your `app.py` file to perform Create and Read operations using our new database model. For `POST` requests, which occur when a user submits a new message, you'll first create a new `Message` object with the submitted `message_text` and `author_name`. Then, you'll add this new message to the database session using `db.session.add(new_message)` and commit the transaction using `db.session.commit()`. This saves the message to your SQLite database. For `GET` requests, which happen when a user simply visits the message board, you'll need to retrieve all messages from the database. You'll achieve this using `messages = Message.query.order_by(Message.date_posted.desc()).all()`, which fetches all messages and orders them by their posting date, newest first. Lastly, to ensure your database tables are created when your application starts, add the `with app.app_context(): db.create_all()` block within the `if __name__ == '__main__':` section of your `app.py` file. This is a crucial step for initializing your database schema. Remember, no significant changes are needed for your `templates/index.html` file, as Jinja2 is smart enough to iterate over the `Message` objects from the database just as it did for the Python list.

segments.text: Welcome to the second part of our hands-on lab.
In this section, you'll modify the `index()` route in your `app.py` file to perform Create and Read operations using our new database model.
For `POST` requests, which occur when a user submits a new message, you'll first create a new `Message` object with the submitted `message_text` and `author_name`.
Then, you'll add this new message to the database session using `db.session.add(new_message)` and commit the transaction using `db.session.commit()`.
This saves the message to your SQLite database.
For `GET` requests, which happen when a user simply visits the message board, you'll need to retrieve all messages from the database.
You'll achieve this using `messages = Message.query.order_by(Message.date_posted.desc()).all()`, which fetches all messages and orders them by their posting date, newest first.

Lastly, to ensure your database tables are created when your application starts, add the `with app.app_context(): db.create_all()` block within the `if __name__ == '__main__':` section of your `app.py` file.
This is a crucial step for initializing your database schema.
Remember, no significant changes are needed for your `templates/index.html` file, as Jinja2 is smart enough to iterate over the `Message` objects from the database just as it did for the Python list.
